entry.title: SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Which notification to use when – Workflow, Situation Handling, KPIs, etc
entry.content:
TL;DR – Know when to use which SAP Fiori notifications.  That is, workflow versus situation handling versus Smart Business KPI subscriptions versus process-specific notifications, and which technique to use if you need to create clean core custom notifications.  

*** Relevant for SAP S/4HANA - all releases ***

A very common business requirement is to notify someone that something has happened and, if possible, get them started on responding to it. 

  • In classic SAP ECC you would use typically workflow notifications and/or email notifications. Unfortunately, over time this often led to a flood of emails, emails being ignored, and increasingly poor response times.
  • In SAP S/4HANA there are a range of more useful, more nuanced, notification techniques available in SAP Fiori that encourage prompt action. You can optionally send them as push notifications to your tablet or phone. These notifications don’t flood your email inbox, however if you want email notifications, you can optionally echo selected notifications to email.

These notifications are deliberately difficult to miss! You will find your notifications in a variety of places, including the notification center of the SAP Fiori launchpad as shown in the example below: 

Why this blog series?  During workshops with one my recent customers currently in transition to SAP S/4HANA, we came across a point of confusion. They are very interested in using Situation Handling but were getting confused about when to use Situation Handling versus Workflow versus some other notification technique. In this blog you will find the different notification techniques explained and when to use them. 

There is a quick summary of the SAP Fiori notification techniques discussed in this blog post in the image below. These techniques are also listed in the table later in this blog post in section SAP Notification Techniques in SAP S/4HANA and when to use them.

In this first blog post, you will learn:

  • Part 1 - SAP Fiori notification techniques available in SAP S/4HANA and when to use them; when to use email notifications to complement or supplement SAP Fiori notifications. 

Later in this blog series you will learn:

  • Part 2 - The impact on business users: SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Which notification to use when – Impact on business users   

In part 2 you will learn where notifications are visible in the SAP Fiori launchpad of SAP S/4HANA and elsewhere such as: SAP Fiori app F0862 My Inbox, SAP Fiori app F6511 My Outbox, SAP Fiori app F4154 My Situations, SAP Fiori app F4537 My Situations - Extended, SAP Build Work Zone,  SAP Task Center, SAP Mobile Start, and elsewhere.

You will also look under the covers at what your team needs to do to enable notifications.

  • Part 3 - For Key Users, Functional Consultants and UX Architects: Where & how to configure each notification technique in SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Which notification to use when – Where and how to configure
  • Part 4 - For Administrators and Developers, understand prerequisites such as the technical notification channel and notification provider that drives predefined and custom notification techniques, what's involved in setting up predefined notifications versus custom notifications, and some FAQ and Troubleshooting tips in SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA – Which notification to use when – Notifications for Admins and Developers

Further references: 

  • For the difference between classic workflows, flexible workflows, and related cloud workflow techniques in SAP BTP refer to SAP Help - ABAP Platform - Workflow
  • For the difference between workflow and situations, and the difference between standard vs extended situations, refer to SAP Help – SAP S/4HANA – Process Management and Integration – Situation Handling - FAQ.
  • For understanding Smart Business KPIs refer to SAP Help - SAP S/4HANA - Analytics - Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
  • Although much has changed, there is still some useful background information in our earlier blog post SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA - Notification Center - Part 1 - Activation 

 

SAP Notification Techniques in SAP S/4HANA and when to use them

In the table below, you will find the 4 main SAP Fiori notification techniques to choose from based on your use case.

Use Case

Example

Notification Technique

Configured By

Notify an approver they have an approvals task

Notify approver of a new Purchase Order requiring their approval

Workflow notifications - flexible workflow (preferred) or classic workflow (supported)

Key User or UX Architect

Notify a business expert of a business situation to be resolved

 

Notify someone that: a contract is about to expire; a batch job has failed with a business-critical error, etc.

Situation Handling notifications - standard or extended

Key User or UX Architect

Notify that a KPI will soon be/has been exceeded target threshold

Notify the responsible manager that actual budget has reached 90% of planned budget

Smart Business KPI notifications

Key User or Analytics Specialist

Notify someone that a process has completed successfully

Notify Purchaser of the number of PRs automatically converted to POs today

Process-specific notifications

Administrator 

When choosing between these notification types the main factors to consider are:

  • Traceability – Where you have very strict highly-controlled processes – such as approvals (also known as delegations of authority) - workflow notifications provide end-to-end traceability of every step of the process. You can find the status of the approval at any time and have an audit trail history (via the workflow log) of what has occurred including who was involved in each task.
  • Productivity – When working with business experts, you want them to know a business situation has happened and to be supported in how to resolve the business situation.  However, you don’t want the business expert to feel micro-managed as that could make them less productive and even impact their mental health!  Situation handling is the right choice here to aid swift resolution while showing that you trust the business expert to take the appropriate action. You can find the status of the situation’s business object at any time, which situation type was triggered, and which team was involved. The user acting on the business object is deliberately not tracked by the situation, however if they have made a change to a business object that will be tracked, as usual, in the change log history of the relevant business object.
  • Expected Response –
    • Workflow notifications require a strict response – for example, the approver must approve or reject a purchase order. 
    • Situation notifications require a flexible response, the business expert must decide what is the appropriate action to take to resolve the situation.
    • Most other notifications – both Smart Business KPIs and process-specific notifications – are primarily about keeping people informed with no specific response needed.
  • Notification source – To make sure the recipient is notified as quickly as possible, it makes sense to trigger the notification from the workflow, situation, KPI or process that first identifies the need for the notification. 
    • Often there are predefined notification providers that provide easy options to configure & trigger these notifications.  
    • Where you don’t have a predefined notification provider, creating a custom notification provider is a relatively easy task for a developer, and worth considering.

 

Understanding the Effort required to Configure Notifications

Skills needed for configuring all predefined notification use cases are LOW. 

Creating your own custom notifications is a LOW to MEDIUM effort for a Developer with a small amount of configuration required by an Administrator.

 

When to use email notifications instead of SAP Fiori notifications

There are 2 additional notification use cases that commonly occur. While they may seem like separate notification types, they are essentially just variations of the notification types listed above. In these cases, an email notification is more likely to be required. These also are LOW effort to configure. 

 

Use Case

Example

How to Handle

Configured By

Notify a casual employee that something has occurred

Notify a user who doesn’t login very often

 

User needs to login at least to the SAP Fiori launchpad. They can go to their personal Settings & opt to echo notifications to email. That is, in the User Actions > Settings > Notifications area. They can only configure notification types they have received at least once.

Business User

Notify an external person that something has occurred

 

Notify a supplier that a quote has been accepted

 

In this situation, the external person does not have access to the SAP Fiori launchpad.  Where needed, notifications to external suppliers are typically included in process-specific notifications. 

Key User or Functional Consultant

 

Sending aggregated email notifications of SAP Fiori notifications

For notifications where a response is expected, you may want to notify the user by multiple channels.

For workflow notifications the Workflow Extended Notifications (program SWN_SELSEN) is still available and can be scheduled as a batch program. You configure workflow extended notifications transactions SWN_CONFIG and SWNADMIN. You can include a link to SAP Fiori app F0862 My Inbox in the email.

Hint: To minimize searching through emails for past notifications, you should consider adding app F6511 My Outbox to all users who have My Inbox. My Outbox enables users to view the workflow log and task log of workflows they have been involved in, allowing them to see what happened before/after their involvement.

For situations, in app F2947 Manage Situation Types or F5437 Manage Situation Types – Extended, you can configure the option to send an email for aggregated notifications.

Refer to

  • SAP Help – ABAP Platform – SAP Business Workflow Reference Documentation - Extended Notifications for SAP Business Workflow
  • SAP Note 2892592 - WF Notifications: Generate link to My Inbox
  • SAP Note 3589593 - Setting Up Workflow Extended Notification Mail for Specific Multiple Recipients
  • SAP Help – SAP S/4HANA – Process Management and Integration - Situation Handling - Notifications

 

Notification techniques to avoid

Avoid using classic SAP Business Workflow “Display Notification” Tasks  - i.e. Task Type = Notification. These classic notifications are only visible in the classic SAP Office Inbox and have very limited features.

 

Becoming a SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA guru

You’ll find much more on our  SAP Fiori for SAP S/4HANA topic page

entry.title: Designing Value Help Services for the Situation Handling - Extended Framework
entry.content:
Understanding Value Help Services: What They Are and Why They Matter?

Value help services are a cornerstone feature in enhancing user experience by offering context-specific assistance. These services provide users with relevant suggestions and options based on the current situation, making tasks more intuitive and efficient. But what exactly are value help services, and how do they help users? Let's dive into their key functions and benefits.

Key Functions and Benefits of Value Help Services

  • Easing Data Entry
    One of the primary goals of value help services is to simplify data entry. For instance, when inputting data like product lists or options that require predefined choices, these services provide a seamless way to select the appropriate data. This reduces the risk of errors and speeds up the data input process.
  • Use in Situation Handling
    Value help services are particularly useful when it comes to defining condition filters for situation templates and types in the Manage Situation Types - Extended app, as well as in the My Situations – Extended app as part of the filter bar. By offering context-specific suggestions, they help users navigate and interact with the system more efficiently, turning complex tasks into manageable ones.

Let's take a closer look at how these services work with an example. Figure 1 below shows how you can choose a plane type when defining a condition filter in the Manage Situation Types – Extended app. Value help services ensure that when you don't have to manually input each plane type; instead, you can select from a list of predefined options. You also see additional information, such as the total seats of the plane, that help you choose the appropriate plane type.

Throughout this blog, we'll continue to use the plane type value help as an example to illustrate how value help services enhance user experience and streamline processes.


Figure 1: Value Help for Plane Type in Condition Filter dialog in the Manage Situation Types - Extended app 

Designing a Value Help Service

In this section, we explore the design of an value help service, breaking down its key components and steps. This will serve as a foundation for integrating these services into the extended framework for Situation Handling. We’ll use artifacts from the Flight situation object (ID: SITDEMO_FLIGHT), which is included as a demo object in the extended framework. The main components and their relations are shown in Figure 2 below:


Figure 2: Overview on Artifacts for the Value Help Definition

Key Components of an Value Help

  • CDS Views
    • Value Help Source CDS View: Define the source entity that serves as the primary data source for the value help service. This view and its view entities are referenced from the situation object.
    • Value Help Provider CDS View(s): Design one or more CDS views specifically for the value help, which may include additional filters or joins to meet the value help requirements.
      Both the base CDS view as well as the Value Help Provider Views contain annotations that are essential for enhancing the functionality and user experience of value helps.
  • OData Service
    Value helps must be exposed as OData services to be accessible to SAP Fiori applications including their respective Service Definition and Business Service.
  • Situation Object
    Linking the source CDS view in a situation object in the Manage Situation Objects app.

Steps to Design an Value Help Service

1. Define the Value Help Source CDS View

Start by creating the source CDS view, which will serve as the primary data source for your value help. This view should include all relevant fields that users might need for filtering or searching. Below is an example based on the Sitn2DemoFlightVH view provided by SAP:

@ObjectModel.viewType: #CONSUMPTION
@ObjectModel.dataCategory: #VALUE_HELP
define view entity C_Sitn2DemoFlightVH as select from R_Sitn2DemoFlight {
  @Consumption.valueHelpDefinition:[{entity: {name: 'C_Sitn2DemoPlaneVH', element: 'SitnDemoPlaneType'}}]  
      key cast( '' as sit2_demo_plane_type ) as SitnDemoPlaneType
}

This view only serves to reference the value helps for the entity sets it contains – it is not necessary to actually retrieve all field values here, i.e., as shown in the above entity set, it is possible to simply hard-code the field value as ''. The important annotations in this view are the @Consumption.valueHelpDefinition annotations which define the Value Help Provider View (entity.name) and the element (entity.element) in the target entity that is linked to the respective fields (SitnDemoPlaneVH and SitnDemoPlaneType in the example above). For more details, check out the Consumption Annotations page in SAP Help Portal.

2. Create the Value Help Provider View

Next, create a CDS view specifically for the value help.[1] This view may include filters, joins, or additional fields necessary for the value help functionality.

@ObjectModel.viewType: #CONSUMPTION
@ObjectModel.dataCategory: #VALUE_HELP
@ObjectModel.representativeKey: 'SitnDemoPlaneType'
define view entity C_Sitn2DemoPlaneVH as select from R_Sitn2DemoPlane
{
@Search.defaultSearchElement: true
@Search.ranking: #HIGH
key SitnDemoPlaneType,

@Search.defaultSearchElement: true 
@Search.ranking: #LOW
SitnDemoSeatsMaxQty,
... 
}

Besides the SitnDemoPlaneType, that was referenced by the entity.element in the Source CDS View above and must be part of the Value Help Provider View, the view incorporates extra fields like the number of seats available. To enhance user experience, the view can also include optional search annotations.

3. Expose as OData Service

Finally, expose the value help CDS view as an OData service to make it accessible to SAP Fiori applications and other systems consuming OData services. Currently, only OData V2 services are supported that needs to be implemented by using Business Service. Ensure the Service Definition includes the Source CDS View. For the latest S/4 HANA releases, the explicit exposure of all referenced Value Help Provider Views via the @Consumption.valueHelpDefinition annotation is optional as these are autoexposed. Only the Value Help Source CDS View  needs to be exposed ike in the example below:

@EndUserText.label: 'Value help for Situation Demo'
define service C_SITN2DEMOFLIGHTVHSRV {
expose C_Sitn2DemoFlightVH as FlightVH;
// Exposure is optional when properly annotated
// expose C_Sitn2DemoPlaneVH as PlaneVH; 
}

This service definition is afterwards used for the service binding. Please use “OData V2 – UI” as binding type. The result should look like the service binding below:[2]


Figure 3: Service Binding for Value Help Service

Extending a Situation Object with a Value Help

We'll now guide you through the steps to add a value help service in the Manage Situation Objects app. To do so, open your situation object in the Manage Situation Objects app. We are again using the Flight situation object (ID: SITDEMO_FLIGHT) that comes with the extended framework, but with a different service that got exposed using Business Services.

Add a Value Help Service in the Manage Situation Objects App

  1. Create a New Value Help Service
    To add a new value help service, you'll start by clicking the "Create" button in your situation object in the Manage Situation Objects app.
  2. Configure the Value Help Service
    in the Value Help Services section, fill the following fields with the specified values:
    1. Service Protocol Version: Set this to V2.
    2. Service Path: Choose Standard - there are currently no other options available.
    3. Service Binding: Enter the name of the service binding of the value help service you’ve created. In the example shown in Figure 3, this is C_SITN2DEMOFLIGHTVHV2.
    4. Service Version: Use the latest service version from your service binding.In the example shown in Figure 3, this version is 1.
  3. Add Properties.
    Add the entity set of the Source CDS View here, not any of the Value Help Provider Views that are also included in the service. Add the name of the property that you want to use.
     Please note that:
    1. you need to select the Value Help Source CDS View here (FlightVH for our example), not the individual Value Help Provider Views  (PlaneVH for our example).
    2. you have to use the name of the entity set as defined in the Service Definition, not the name of the CDS view, i.e. for our example use FlightVH and not C_Sitn2DemoFlightVH.  
    3. All Entity Sets and Properties are case sensitive! Please use the casing that is exposed in the Service Definition: FlightVH is correct for the example. Other names such as FLIGHTVH are wrong.

The results should look like the figure below:


Figure 4: Manage Situation Objects: add a Value Help Service

Mapping Value Help Entities in the Situation Object Structures

To complete your value help setup, you provide a mapping between the fields of the CDS views you use in the structure of your situation object and the properties in the value help service entities. We'll walk you through the necessary steps to do this below:

  1. Open the Structure in the Manage Situation Objects app
    Navigate to the structure within your situation object that you wish to extend with value help functionality.
  2. Access the Value Help Mapping Section
    Next, go to the "Value Help Mapping" section. This is where you will map the fields to the value help entities.
  3. Create a New Mapping
    1. Click on the "Create" button to add a new value help mapping.
    2. Select a Field: Choose the field from the structure that you want to enhance with a value help. For our example, we're using SITNDEMOPLANETYPE.
    3. Assign the Value Help
      After selecting the field, use the value help to select the value help ID you modeled in the previous steps. Ensure you match the entity set and property correctly. For our example, the mapping should be:
      Value Help ID: VALUE_HELP_DEMO
      Entity Set: FlightVH
      Property: SitnDemoPlaneType
    4. Again all Entity Sets and Properties are case sensitive! Please use the casing that is exposed in the Service Definition: FlightVH is correct for the example. Other names such as FLIGHTVH are wrong.

The results should look like the figure below:


Figure 5: Manage Situation Objects: mapping of Value Help Service and Structure fields

By following these steps, you'll successfully add the value help service to your situation object, enhancing your ability to manage situations effectively.

Using the Situation Object Enhanced with Value Help Services

Once you've created your situation objects and enhanced them with value help services, they're ready for use in situation scenarios, situation templates, and situation types. Most of your defined content is automatically propagated, making changes—even in value help services—immediately active.

However, situation type updates are handled different due to performance caching. If you add value help services after creating a situation type, you'll need to refresh it by creating a new version of the situation type. You can do this by making a small change for example in the type description and saving afterwards. This will trigger the value help changes to become active. For any situation type you create after enhancing your situation objects, the changes will immediately be applied.

Tips and tricks for testing and in case of problems

Testing your value help service

To test if your value help service works correctly you can first test OData Service itself and afterward test the value service in the context of the Situation Handling Framework.

To test the OData Service service, open the Service Binding for your value help service and right click on the Entity Set (FlightVH) and select  the "Open Fiori Elements App Preview" option as show in the figure below. 

Figure 6: Testing the value help service: generate the Fiori Elements App Preview from the entity set.

In app that is opened in your browser, click on the "Adapt Filters" button and select the filter you want to test. Afterward check if the value help for the filter in the generated app is what is expected. 


Figure 7: Testing the value help service in the Fiori Elements App Preview app 

Afterwards you can test the service in the Situation Handling context. Therefore create a new situation template that makes use of the situation object[3] that you’ve defined and check the condition filters. Make sure to select the correct trigger or anchor object for the condition filter to see all fields and their value helps.
An example for the Demo Scenario is shown in Figure 1 Value Help for Plane Type in Condition Filter dialog in the Manage Situation Types - Extended app.

Check the $metadata of your value help service

When the value helps are not working, please check the $metadata of your service. All fields with value help services should have the <Annotation Term="Common.ValueList"> property.

An example is the $metadata of the Demo Application

URL: …/sap/opu/odata/sap/C_SITN2DEMOFLIGHTVH_CDS/$metadata 

<Annotation Term="Common.ValueList">
...
<Record>
<PropertyValue Property="CollectionPath" String="C_Sitn2DemoRegionVH" />
...
</Annotations>

Similar annotation should be available in the OData Service defined in the Service Binding. Simply extend the service URL with /$metadata and check the properties you annotated. There should be a Common.ValueList annotation for each field annotated with @Consumption.valueHelpDefinition in your Source CDS View.

Case sensitivity for Entity Sets and Properties

Entity Sets and Properties are case sensitive and need to be used consistently.

Creating or Updating Situation Types after Situation Object Changes

As mentioned earlier (section “Using the Value Help enhanced objects”) remember that situation objects are cached for performance reasons in situation types when the situation type is created. This means that changes in the situation object are not reflected for the existing situation types, even if you might see them already in the situation template, unless they are updated.
So, whenever an update of situation objects was required, please remember to change or create new situation types to reflect the changes.

Update structure mapping after changing Value Help Services

Whenever you update a value help service in a situation object, , make sure to also update the value help mapping in the respective structure of the situation object.
Figure 6 shows an example where the entity set is wrong (ZAS_VH_BASE_VIEW) and should be changed to the correct name of the entity set as it’s exposed in the service (-> FlightVH). Once this was changed in the Value Help section, it also needs to be changed in the Value Help Mapping in the Structure section(s). The figure show the wrong configuration that is using the view (ZAS_VH_BASE_VIEW) instead of the correct view entity as exposed in the service definition (FlightVH for our example). Please ensure that the Entity Set is changed in both locations in the Value Help Section as well as in the Value Help Mapping and that both Entity Set and Properties are the same. The correct configuration should showFlightVH in both Entity Sets. 


Figure 8: Manage Situation Object: Reflect changes in Value Help also to the Structure Mapping.

Popup “No authorization to access value help for <<FIELDNAME>> . Please define conditions”

While using the condition filter dialog, you might encounter the following error:
Figure 9: Popup “No authorization to access value help for <<FIELDNAME>> . Please define conditions”

This error can arise from two primary issues:

  1. Value Help Service Authorization: There may be an authorization problem with the value help service, which needs to be addressed in the backend – check the DCLs assigned to the views and the authorizations given to the user.
  2. Service Issues: The service itself might be experiencing problems.

Troubleshooting Steps:
To diagnose if the issue is with the service, use the browser’s network tab in the debugging tools to check for a /$metadata request related to your value help service.
Here’s what you might find:

  • Service Not Published: If the service URL is unavailable, it’s likely that the service hasn’t been published. Ensure that the service is properly published.
  • Wrong OData Version: If you see an error message similar to
<code>/IWFND/MED/170</code>
<message xml:lang="en">No service found for namespace '', name '...', version '0001'</message>
<innererror>​

it’s probable that the incorrect OData version was used. Ensure you are using “OData V2 – UI” as specified in the “Expose as OData Service” step in the section “Steps to Design an Value Help Service.”

By following these steps, you should be able to identify and resolve the underlying issue causing the error.

Conclusion

Modeling value help services for the extended framework for Situation Handling is a powerful way to enhance user experience by providing context-specific assistance. By following the principles and best practices demonstrated in the Flight Demo, experienced developers can create robust and effective value help services tailored to their projects.
Stay tuned for more advanced techniques and in-depth discussions as we continue to explore the capabilities of the extended framework for Situation Handling.
Happy coding!

Footnotes:

[1] Multiple Value Help Provider Views need to be created when the source CDS view references several Value Help Provider Views in the annotations.
[2]  Note -This service does not exist in the Flight situation object that uses a different mechanism. However, the target design is to use service bindings.
[3]  When creating the situation template, you first need to create a situation scenario where the situation object that is enhanced with value help services is used as trigger or anchor object. The value help becomes visible in the value help for the field it got assigned to in the condition’s filters of the trigger or anchor object.

entry.title: Deprecation of Intelligent Situation Automation Service
entry.content:
Abstract

Intelligent Situation Automation is an extension of Situation Handling. It processes situations and resolves them automatically using established business rules, thereby reducing the time users spend on routine, manual, and repetitive tasks. Please refer to SAP Discovery Center for more information. 

As part of this blog, we are announcing the deprecation of Intelligent Situation Automation service. 

 

 

What is the current end-of-service date of Intelligent Situation Automation? 

The Intelligent Situation Automation will be under maintenance only mode and the end-of-service date is 6 months from the announcement or when the last contract commitment is fulfilled. 

 

What do you need to do? 

Unsubscribe the Intelligent Situation Automation SaaS solution. Please refer to below steps:

Prerequisite: You are an administrator of the subaccount.

  1. Open your global account in the SAP BTP cockpit and open your subaccount.
  2. In the navigation area of each subaccount, choose Services > Instances and Subscriptions.
  3. Select the three dots at the end of the Intelligent Situation Automation subscription row, and from the menu, select Delete. All data related to the application will be deleted in the respective subaccount.

     

If you have any questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to contact us via component CA-SIT-ATM.

entry.title: S/4HANA Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) and Situation Handling Scenarios: Part-1
entry.content:
In this blog, Part-1, I will be primarily focusing on SAP Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management (ISLM) through a Supply Chain use case - predicting the forecast delivery date by using regression based predictive model (SAP Standard ISLM Framework). This Model provides predictions based on historical data. I will also touch base on the SAP Situation Handling Scenario for the Stock Transfer Order Process. However, I will walk you through the set-up in more detail in Part-2 of this blog series.

My Business Use Case:

My organization has to transfer an Asset: 20000000 (Equipment: 10000001-Air Compressor 1250 CFM 8KG/CM2) from our Norco Plant in Louisiana to our Robinson Plant in Illinois. To support this process and predict the forecast delivery date based on historical stock transfers, we have activated the ISLM Scenario: MATERIAL_OVERDUE_SIT (Stock In Transit Material Overdue) and a  Situation Handling Scenario: MAN_MATLOVERDUESITSITN (Stock Transport Order Overdue) to monitor exceptions as well.

Let us dive in...

What Is ISLM: Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management is a standardized framework to build and manage AI use cases within SAP S/4HANA for both embedded and side-by-side scenarios. It can be leveraged to perform lifecycle operations, including Scheduled Training and Retraining, and deployment of the model directly within SAP S/4HANA.

ISLM framework consists of two Fiori Applications, Intelligent Scenarios (App ID F4469) and Intelligent Scenario Management (App ID F4470). These two applications provide a unified interface for creating, deploying,  monitoring, and activation of the model directly within SAP S/4HANA.

Based on the ISLM association with business application, the ISLM scenarios can be categorized as Embedded and Side-by-Side.

Embedded: A business application, for example SAP S/4HANA runs in the same stack as its machine learning provider with the analytics libraries SAP HANA Automated Predictive Library (APL) or SAP HANA Predictive Analysis Library (PAL).

 Side-by-Side: A business application, for example SAP S/4HANA runs in a separate stack than its machine learning infrastructure provider.

 To begin with, let us take a look at the architecture of SAP Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management.

Architecture of Intelligent Scenario Lifecycle Management

  • Business User: The user who Interacts with the business application and uses the predictions from machine learning for the business purpose.
  • Business Administrator: A domain expert who can perform model trainings based on business context, evaluate model quality , and activate a model for production usage.
  • Technical Administrator: A system administrator who can perform the configurations of connectivity between different entities and maintains the technical configurations of the system.
  • ABAP Developer: A developer who can create ABAP artifacts required for Intelligent Scenario registration.
  • Intelligent Scenario Owner: An owner who creates, reviews, and publishes the Intelligent Scenario.

For instance, based on our business use case, I will walk you through the standard ISLM scenario that leverages one of the models from SAP HANA Automated Predictive Library (APL) by stepping into the roles of "Business User", "Business Administrator", and "Intelligent Scenario Owner".

The Intelligent Scenarios App is used to create, display, and configure various scenarios tailored to specific business needs. Using this App, we can view a list and activate SAP provided standard scenarios or create Embedded or Side-by-Side scenarios. 

Now, let us use the SAP provided ISLM scenario "MATERIAL_OVERDUE_SIT" and take a look at the input and out put fields used by the model, and Fiori App IDs that support the business process.

The Input fields are the data points to train an ML model and to make new prediction. They represent the historical business data and other relevant information that the ML model can learn from to identify the patterns.

Output fields contain the results generated by the ML model after it is trained. These output fields provide the predictions and related metrics back to the business application.

It`s time to publish the scenario...

After successfully publishing the ISLM scenario, let us move on to the "Intelligent Scenario Management" application to  train the model and schedule it.

The Intelligent Scenario Management App is used to manage, monitor,  and optimize AI driven scenarios throughout their entire lifecycle. We can view the list of App IDs relevant for the ISLM scenario MATERIAL_OVERDUE_SIT.

For instance, let us retrain the model with new historical data using new filtering conditions. The system generates a new Model Version ID for every "Retrain".

Following the successful training, the system provides a statistical information on variables and performance of the model. The model version report screen provides a summary about a particular model version. The quality information details varies according to the intelligent scenario type and underlying machine learning used.

For Instance, the following filter values are used for training the model.

The tab "Debrief" in a "Model Version Report" provides a breakdown of the trained machine learning model`s characteristics and its key influencing factors. The "Debrief" helps us understand and evaluate the model by explaining the main drivers behind its prediction.

Key Influencers and their percentage of contribution in the overall prediction.

We can schedule a training for our Intelligent Scenarios. When the schedule is created for a training, the system creates a planned task, which can be viewed in "Scheduled Planned Task" tab.

Mini Note: If we try to create a new schedule without deactivating the previous one, the system prompts an error message.

We can monitor the scheduled runs that are created via ISLM in the "Monitor Planned Task Jobs" tile.

We can copy and cancel the planned task and view the logs associated with each run of the schedule.

Now, let us move on to "Situation Handling Scenarios"...

As part of our business use case, I have activated the situation handling scenario with the following conditions: "MAN_MATLOVERDUESITSITN" to notify respective business team if the the order gets delayed.

Situation Handling Scenario: ZMAN_MATLOVERDUESITSITN conditions to trigger an exception message.

Situation Handling Conditions to trigger an exception notification...

Following the successful activation and training of ISLM and Situation Handling Scenarios, let us examine the transactional data.

Norco Plant asset/equipment master:

We have Asset Master and Equipment Master synchronization functionality in place. 

Following the successful movement of equipment 10000001 from its functional location to Engineering Spares Warehouse, the system updates the stock in the designated storage location, which should be transferred to the Robinson Plant.  The stock movement has been completed using a Maintenance Order.

Now, let us create a Stock Transfer Order using App ID F1957 - Transfer Stock Cross - Plant

With this App, we can make transfer postings from one plant(Issuing Plant) to another plant(Receiving Plant). This app supports warehouse clerk in finding the allowed transfer postings  and in personalizing the control settings of storage locations and visible columns.

For instance, I have chosen the material code "271", which is designated for Equipment 10000001.

Mini Note: If the predictive analytics model is active, the system uses the predicted delivery date as forecast delivery date. We can also select the entry "Use Predictive Model for Forecast Delivery Date" in the application settings.

I have chosen the storage location 171B , which contains the stock of Equipment 10000001. I have entered the input values in the pop-up screen. The activated ISLM scenario model determines the "Forecast Delivery Date" for the stock transfer order based on the historical data.

Now, let us create "Stock Transport Order" using the option "Create Stock Transport Order".

Following the successful creation of stock transport order,  using App ID F2139: Overdue Materials - Stock In Transit, we can view the "Predicted Deviation" values for the stock transport orders.

Using this App F2139 (Overdue Materials-Stock In Transit) with an Active Predictive Model:

  • If the predictive analytical model is active, the system uses the predicted delivery date as forecast delivery date.
  • If the predictive analytics model is active, we can select the "Predicted Deviation" field in the view settings for the results list.

Mini Note: The predicted deviation field displays the difference between the planned and the predicted delivery date. With this information about the predicted deviation, we get an impression that if a goods receipt can be successfully completed in time.

How to Interpret the predicted Deviation field value:

  • In our case, the predicted deviation for the STO 4500000334 is negative, i.e., -1  : This means that the forecast delivery date calculated by the predictive model is one day later than the planned delivery date from the purchase order.
  • If the predicted deviation is 0 (Zero) : This means that the forecast delivery date and the planned delivery date from the purchase order are the same.
  • If the predicted deviation is positive, for example 2 : This means that the forecast delivery date calculated by the predictive model is two days ahead of the planned delivery date from the purchase order.

Using this App F2139 (Overdue Materials-Stock In Transit) without an Active Predictive Model: 

  • If the predictive analytics model is not active, we cannot select the "Predicted Deviation" field in the view settings for the results list.
  • If the predictive analytics model is not active, the micro chart uses the planned delivery date from the purchase order instead.
  • If the predictive analytics model is not active, the forecast delivery date and the planned delivery date of the purchase order are the same.

The shipping duration micro chart illustrates the goods movement process for an Stock Transfer Order item and shows the forecast delivery date in relation to the actual delivery date. 

Since we have activated the "Situation Handling Scenario" with the conditions, the system triggers the exception notification when the stock in transit days are >1.

In our use case, the STO 4500000334 was delayed and met the conditions that are part of situation handling scenario; hence, the system triggered the exception notification.

The situations are displayed at "Bell Icon", which is a gate way to the SAP Fiori notification center.

or we can use "App ID: F4154 (My Situations app) " to monitor exception notifications.

Following the successful completion of the STO 4500000334, the situation can be closed using thee option "Close Situations" in My Situations App.

I hope this blog proves useful to the Inventory Management team to have a nuanced understanding of material movements with enhanced predictive insights and exception notifications during Stock Transfer Order Process.

What is Situation Handling Scenario:

In a nut shell, SAP Situation Handling Scenario helps organizations increase the quality and efficiency of the business processes by automatically detecting, tracking, and informing the right users about the exceptional circumstances that require their immediate attention. With its tracking and monitoring features, Situation Handling allows organization to get insights into the life cycle of situations and to  identify the recurring situations that can be prevented or automatically resolved.

Let us dive in...

To begin with, let us understand the Key Concepts of Situation Handling Scenario.

  • Situation Template: It serves as a blueprint for creating a situation type.
  • Situation Type: It describes the business situation. For example, how a situation instance can be triggered and who is informed about it.
  • Situation Instance: An exceptional issue which is displayed the responsible person.
  • Situation object: Technical model of a business object used in Situation Handling. It provides the basic technical configuration such as data structures, events, and actions.
  • Situation Scenario: Business Scenario that contains defining entity sets to create multiple situation templates.

Disclaimer: This blog focuses on the Situation Handling Standard Framework.

entry.title: Handling Maintenance Notifications with SAP Situation Handling
entry.content:
Efficient maintenance management is critical for smooth operations in any enterprise. SAP’s Situation Handling framework provides a proactive way to keep stakeholders informed and enable quick actions when key events occur. In this blog, we’ll explore how to leverage the Manage Situation Types – Extended app to handle maintenance notifications effectively.

 

What is Situation Handling in SAP?

Situation Handling in SAP helps users stay informed about important business events by triggering notifications and enabling them to take quick actions. For Enterprise Asset Management (EAM), SAP provides standard situation templates that can be customized to meet your business needs.

For more details and advanced configuration, refer to the official SAP Cookbook.

Template Name: EAM_MAINT_NOTIF_SUBPHASE_CHANGED

Description: Notification Subphase is changed

This template supports both event-based and batch-based triggers for maintenance notifications when they are:

  • Created
  • In Process
  • Completed

Key Features of the Template

  • Perform quick callback actions like Accept or Reject a maintenance notification.
  • Navigate to the Manage Maintenance Notification (F5777) app for detailed actions.
  • Configure recipients who should receive notifications via email or SAP Fiori Launchpad (FLP).

 

Steps to Configure Situation Handling for Maintenance Notifications

1. Create a Situation Type from the Standard Template

Select the template Notification Subphase is changed and click Create Situation Type.

 

2. Define Situation Triggers

Under the Situation Triggers tab, configure when notifications should be triggered. The template supports:

  • Event-Based Triggers for real-time updates (e.g., when a notification is created or completed).
  • Batch-Based Triggers for scheduled checks.

 

3. Configure Recipients

Under the Recipients section, assign users or teams who should receive notifications. You can filter recipients by Responsibility Definition (e.g., Lead, Internal) defined in the Teams and Responsibilities app.

 

4. Customize Notification Messages

End users can configure the message text shown in notifications for better clarity and context.

5. Define Conditions for Situation Trigger

Under the Conditions tab, you can set filters to control when the situation should be triggered. This allows fine-grained control over notifications.

You can filter based on:

  • Creation Date
  • Equipment
  • Functional Location
  • Last Changed By
  • Notification Text
  • Person Responsible
  • Priority (e.g., only trigger for Very High priority)
  • Phase or Subphase

 

6. Access My Situations – Extended App

Use this app to view all notifications raised, quick details of the maintenance notification, and perform quick actions like Accept Maintenance Notification or Navigate to the Manage Maintenance Notification app.

 

Benefits of Using Situation Handling for Maintenance Notifications

  • Proactive Alerts: Stay informed about critical changes in maintenance notifications.
  • Quick Actions: Accept or reject notifications directly from the alert.
  • Role-Based Notifications: Ensure the right people are notified at the right time.
  • Flexibility: Define conditions and customize messages to suit business needs.

Conclusion

By leveraging SAP’s Situation Handling and the Manage Situation Types – Extended app, organizations can streamline maintenance processes, reduce delays, and improve operational efficiency. Start by creating a situation type from the standard template and configure triggers, recipients, and messages to fit your requirements.

References

For more details and advanced configuration, refer to the official SAP Cookbook: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_CLOUD/a630d57fc5004c6383e7a81efee7a8bb/516c8ecb7462453ca430a42481cc33ec.html?version=2508.500

entry.title: My First Situation with the Extended Framework
entry.content:
Situation Handling notifies users about issues requiring their attention. With the extended framework for Situation Handling, you can define situations for your business needs.

This blog post illustrates how you can create a situation quickly and with minimal configuration. It outlines the core concept of the extended framework for Situation Handling and guides you in defining your own situation use case.

The configuration relates to the extended framework for Situation Handling which has been available since SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2202 and SAP S/4HANA 2021 FPS2.

 

Introductory Words

The extended framework for Situation Handling is very powerful. In turn, it’s not always easy to get started. To provide you with a straightforward path, this blog post focuses on the minimal viable configuration to create a situation instance.

The Apps

The configuration of Situation Handling is set up across three apps to maximize reuse. While it may seem complex at first, the advantages become clear as you create multiple use cases. The configuration effort decreases substantially with each new use case. The apps also align with different business roles supporting technical and business-oriented responsibilities.

  • Manage Situation Objects – reuse the artifacts from the applications, such as CDS views, events, and navigation targets, for defining a situation object.
  • Manage Situation Scenarios – map the affected object (anchor object) with trigger objects and trigger behaviors create, update, and remove.
  • Manage Situation Types – add logic to the anchor and trigger objects to define the use case

To inform the right users we additionally use the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app.

The Use Case

The extended framework for Situation Handling also comes with a demo app that serves as exploratory sandbox. We use the Situation Handling Demo app and its artifacts for the minimal configuration.

The demo app represents a fictional flight booking system. Your first situation will inform about flights that are scheduled within the next three days.

 

Minimal Configuration

Let’s define the minimal set-up to create a situation.

Manage Situation Objects

The situation object represents a business object. It reuses existing application artifacts that are relevant to your business scope. The core of a situation object is the structure, a CDS view. The CDS view needs to be allowlisted and needs a unique key.

Log-in as Extensibility Specialist to your system and open the app Manage Situation Objects.

Create a new object and enter the object ID, the name, description, and select the SAP object type.

General information of situation object

Then you add the CDS view that contains the data you want to monitor. The CDS view is part of the object’s structure. Create a new structure and enter a description. Select the structure type, the structure name (the reference to the CDS view), and the SAP object node type. For personal data simply select no fields.

CDS structure of situation object

Additionally, you add the semantic key that represents the situation object on the UI. For the flight object we choose the carrier ID, the connection ID and the flight date from the object’s CDS view. It will show, for example, as LH/403/20251224.

Then choose Apply and Create. Your first situation object is set.

Manage Situation Scenarios

The situation scenario relates to the object that is affected by a situation (anchor object). Additionally, it contains the objects that can trigger a situation.

Background:  The trigger object can be the same as the anchor object - for example, if you want to monitor the data of the anchor object’s CDS view. The trigger object can also be another situation object. In our flight example, the trigger object could be the booking object, and the anchor object is the flight.

The trigger object also comes with a trigger behavior. The trigger object can be created or updated; it can also be removed.

In our example, we use the Flight object, both as anchor and as trigger object with the behavior add / update.

Open the app Manage Situation Scenarios.

Create a new scenario with ID, name, and description. Provide the scenario type and the object structure type. You also select the responsibility context ID which links Responsibility Management to Situation Handling to be able to identify the right users who need to be informed about the situation.

General information of situation scenario

Then you add the reference to the object that is affected by the situation, the anchor object. Select the object ID. Chose the object structure ID (an object can have multiple structures) and a key field that uniquely identifies your anchor object. The key field is part of the structure’s CDS view.

Reference to anchor object

Next you define the situation trigger with name and description. As we want to check the CDS fields regularly we create a batch-based trigger.

Batch-based situation trigger

Finally, you need to add the reference to the trigger object like you did for the anchor object. Select the object ID, the object structure ID, and the object key field. Additionally select the relevant object behavior. In our example, it’s add/update because we want to monitor flight data that is new or changed.

Reference to trigger object

Choose Apply and Create. Your scenario is done.

Log-off as Extensibility Specialist and log-in as Business Process Configuration Expert.

Manage Situation Types – Extended

In the  Manage Situation Types – Extended app you define the logic when a situation is detected and who should be informed about it.

Background: The app supports the idea of reuse as well. You can create a situation template that serves as blueprint. And you can derive multiple situation types from it. The blueprint, for example, defines the monitoring of flights. Flight monitoring may require different conditions for different regions. For this purpose, you can derive multiple situation types from the template that contain all settings from the blueprint. You only need to adjust the conditions for the specific regions.

In our use case we want to identify flights that are scheduled within the next three days. Therefore, we want to check the flight data daily and use the batch-based situation trigger from the scenario. In the condition section we define the relevant period of next 3 days.

Open the app Manage Situation Types – Extended.

Create a new template from the scenario My First Scenario. Enter general data that describes the template: the scenario ID, the template ID, the name, and description.

General information of situation template

Then you add the batch-based trigger from the scenario and refine it with conditions. For our use case we simply add a date filter for the next three days.

Condition for situation detection

Now we add the texts that describe the situation for the end user. The situation title and description are used in various places, for example, in My Situations – Extended app, in cards on Fiori launchpad home, and in notifications. We define the title and only use variables to the flight for describing the situation. If we choose to send one notification per situation instance, the same texts are used. The public text My first situation. is added for email notifications (not visible in screenshot).

Situation description for end users

Select Apply.

In the next step we define when the periodical check is scheduled. We define a time zone, a repeat type and interval, and add a start time when the batch is supposed to be scheduled. In the example below, the batch is scheduled every day at 1 am.

Batch-job scheduling

Then we need to define who will be informed about situations. We want to alert users that belong to one or more teams that are responsible for a certain business scope which is expressed by the team category. We use the demo category SITDEMO. Without setting any further filters, all members of the teams belonging to the category would be informed about flights being scheduled within the next three days.

Inform team members about situations

Select Create and your template is complete.

Manage Teams and Responsibilities

Responsibility Management defines who is informed about the situation. Let’s create a simple team and add yourself as a team member.

Open the app Manage Teams and Responsibilities.

Create a new team and enter general data that describes the team: the name (that is also used as global ID), the description, and the type. The type is a sub-group of the team category. Also ensure that you set the status to enabled.

Define a responsible team

Then you add the team members that will be informed about the situations. For the minimal configuration you just add yourself as member.

Members of responsible team

Create the team and log-off as Business Process Configuration Expert.

Log-in as Business Configuration Specialist.

Situation Handling Demo

You can use the data of the Situation Handling Demo app to create a situation. Just open the app and check if the table is already populated with flight data. If not, choose Generate New Data.

Situation Handling Demo app

Manage Situation Types – Extended

Now you create a situation type from the template that will trigger the situation. Usually, types would be further refined or would be a bundle of variants to reflect specific usage. For example, the logic of a template refers to multiple types which address specific sales regions and therefore need specific adjustments in the condition section. In our sample case we simply use the logic of the template as is.

Open the Manage Situation Types – Extended app.

Create a new situation type from the template My First Template. Set the status to enabled and save it.

General information of situation type

On top of the page choose Trigger Batch.

Trigger the batch-job schedule for a situation type

 

Batch-job feedback

In the dialog select Manage Instances. You might need to wait a moment until the batch-job is finalized and refresh the page. Then you see the list of detected situations, that is all flights that are scheduled within the next three days. As a reference you see the semantic keys that you defined within the situation object structure.

List of situation instances in the Manage Situation Types – Extended app

Log-off as Business Process Specialist.

My Situations – Extended

In the My Situation – Extended app the users see all situations in their area of responsibility.

Log-in with the user you added as team member in the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app.

Open the My Situation – Extended  app.

In the left navigation pane select the scenario My First Situation Scenario. The list shows all situations that were detected by the type My First Situation Type. The title My First Situation is the same for all instances. In the description you see the reference to the detected flight, for example, SQ 0160 13.12.2025.

Additionally, you see the new situations indicated next to the notification bell.

List of situations in the My Situations – Extended app

When you select a situation, for example in the list page of the My Situation – Extended app or from the notifications, you go to the situation details page. As the situation description is all we defined, there is no further information to see.

Situation details page in the My Situations – Extended app

You have created your first situations with the minimal configuration. And you have learned which minimal ingredients you need and how they work together.

Next Steps

For further guidance, I recommend reading the following blog posts:

  • Define the optimal information for the end user: Configure the layout of My Situations – Extended.
  • Deep dive into the concept of reusability: The Power of Reuse - Custom Situation Configuration.
  • Explore enhanced configuration options: Custom Situation Cases: Configure Your Own Use Cases.

You find many more blog posts in the Best Practices section of Intelligent Situation Handling in the SAP Community. And you can visit SAP Help for further guidance on Situation Handling.

entry.title: The Top 5 Things You Always Wanted to Know About Situation Handling
entry.content:
Situation Handling let’s you alert appropriate users about critical business issues requiring their attention. If you're curious about how it works or need more details, this blog post is for you. Additionally, we've enhanced our documentation - be sure to take a look here: Documentation.

1)    How does it really work?

Situation Handling detects business issues in your systems. The detection works for issues with either business objects or error and warning messages. In the following, these will simply be referred to as “objects”. An issue is typically defined by specific conditions or events happening that are assigned to the objects.  – and then, voilà, either a routine daily batch run or business event monitoring identifies the objects with issues.* It can be, for example, an expiring sales contract, an overbooked flight, and many more. This leads to the next question:

2)    How do I specify the business issues to be addressed by Situation Handling? How is the setup done?

Let’s understand this first: Situation Handling can detect issues from only one object or between two associated objects. If only one object is involved, that’s quite easy – the object triggering an issue, with certain conditions or events, is the very same object that helps to solve it by changing itself in a specific app. One example would be a sales quotation that has expired and needs to be checked for purchase details in order to get back to the customers.

How two associated objects work: One is usually triggering the situation. For example, the situation is triggered because the object is newly created, extends a certain value, or expires. The other object is the one that needs to be changed because it’s the one affected. This is also called the anchor object, as it “anchors” the situation. For example, a change in the processor may cause a purchasing document item to require a review. Alternatively, missing supplier confirmations make operational purchasers check the schedule lines of purchase order items again.

For the Situation Handling engine to detect situations, it needs to know what to look for. The objects with their conditions, events, and possible mappings between them need to be defined. Your business area may have very specific business issues – we got you covered with a wide range of ready-to-use situation templates. They are called “templates” because elements (like conditions) are predefined, while others (like condition filters or your specific situation texts) can be adapted by you. Just copy a template into your personal situation type and enable it.

I can already anticipate your next question: What if my case is not on the list? No problem at all – with our new framework, you can define all parts of Situation Handling yourself. It’s called “extended framework” because of its extended functionalities.

3)    And how do I alert someone? This seems complicated.

I’m not gonna lie, it seems complicated. It’s seems complicated at first, because we’ve provided all the different ways to alert someone that we (and you!) could possibly think of. First, your company’s organizational structure – a lot of customers want to alert specific team members based on their job functions. But we also offer the possibility to alert people depending on the data a situation provides – for example, the creator of a sales order, its processor, or other field values. For more information, check out the documentation.

4)    Let me try it 🤩

Now you must be wondering: Can I check this out? Sure – all SAP S/4HANA, SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, and SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition customers have Situation Handling included. Just assign the “Business Process Specialist” role to your user and open the “Manage Situation Types” app. Our situation template “Sales Order Is Close to Expiry” is auto-activated, which means you can immediately check it out under “Situation Types”.

If you want to try setting up something very simple, we recommend following the test script from SAP Best Practices of our Situation Handling scope item (31N)  under “Accelerators”. If you’re more interested in our extended framework, we’ve even built three demo situation templates and our own demo app for creating dummy data. Check it out in this blog post.

5)    Uff… I have issues (and I don’t mean my business issues 😫). I did all the setup, and Situation Handling doesn’t seem to work. No one gets alerted.

No worries at all. There’s already a very well-written blog post that provides a lot of guidance.

6)    What next?

Interested? Great. We have a lot more to offer.

  • Let’s get started 😊 Check out all situation templates to see if any fit your business issues. For the setup, check out Getting Started.
  • Already a pro? Check out how you can improve your Situation Handling by monitoring it and changing certain parameters in this blog post.
  • Interested in AI? Stay tuned 😎
  • Need more help with Responsibility Management and alerting relevant users? There’s also a blog post series available.
  • Start creating your custom use cases (if you haven’t done so already): Blog post

Last but not least: I’m one of your technical writers for Situation Handling. Not only do I provide you with six steps when you only expected five, I’m also always happy to help 🫡This is our documentation (quick link: http://help.sap.com/s4_ce_situationhandling for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition and http://help.sap.com/s4_op_situationhandling for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition/SAP S/4HANA) and we love to hear your feedback.

Don’t forget to comment on anything you didn’t get, missed, would have loved to explore further – I promise, we will react! And of course, comment on all the things you liked – then we know what to keep. Thank you 🫶

More questions? Comment on this blog post, and we will try to answer them 😊

@Christiane_Poreski 
@angelika_salmen 
@sebastian_doeweling 
@axel_spriestersbach 
@Dr_Joerg_Rett 
@VidyaShetty 
@NisargaPuttegowda 

_____

* For sure, monitoring business events is way more elegant than a batch run, as it catches issues right away (with some delay due to system load though, but still fairly recent). But obviously, not all conditions can be detected through events, so a once-a-day batch run is performed on the objects to identify those with issues. A batch run also has its advantages, for example, it sends controlled information once a day with no spam by frequent events.

entry.title: How Do I Activate a Situation Type in the Extended Framework?
entry.content:
Situation Handling notifies users about issues requiring their attention. You may choose SAP delivered situation templates or design your own use cases. For the extended framework for Situation Handling, we often discussed how you can create custom situation templates. The framework comes also with SAP delivered use cases that you can easily activate.

This blog post explains how you can activate situation types from SAP delivered situation templates with the extended framework for Situation Handling. It has been available since SAP S/4HANA Cloud 2202 and SAP S/4HANA 2021 FPS02.

 

SAP Delivered Use Cases

Looking for Situation Handling use cases? Visit SAP Help and navigate to Situation Handling, then choose Use Cases. You can narrow your results by filtering for Situation Template Type (either extended object-based or message-based), area, and topic. To learn more about a specific use case, simply check the link in the Situation Template column for a detailed description.

Use Case

For illustration purposes we use the situation template Expiration of Purchase Contracts (PROC_ABOUT_TO_EXPIRE_CTR). Purchasers get a heads-up for purchase contracts that are about to expire.

 

Activation Overview for 2SL and 3SL

Before discussing the activation steps in detail, let me point out the differences between system landscapes and their specific transport paths.

In the extended framework for Situation Handling, you create a situation type from a situation template. Situation templates are only visible in the quality system of a 2-system landscape (2SL) and the development system of a  3-system-landscape (3SL). The situation type needs to be transported to the production system. The transport paths differ between 2SL and 3SL.

Transport the Situation Type in 2SL

In a 2-system-landscape, you transport the situation type from the quality system to the production system.

  • In the quality system you
    • Create a situation type from a situation template
    • Test if the configuration alerts the right users about the situation
    • Export the well-defined situation type
  • In the production system you
    • Import the situation type
    • Since the data usually differs between quality and production system you need to enter the appropriate values for the condition filters
    • Enable the situation type

Transports in 2-System-Landscape

Transport the Situation Type in 3SL

In a 3-system-landscape, transports are required from the development system to both the test and production system. In a 3SL environment you may also have different tenants for development, customizing, and parallel customizing that need to be considered as well.

  • On the customizing tenant in the development system you
    • Create a situation type from a situation template
    • Export the situation type
  • On the test tenant in the test system you
    • Import the situation type
    • Since the data usually differs between systems you need to enter the appropriate values for the condition filters
    • Test if the configuration alerts the right users about the situation
    • Forward the well-defined situation type
  • On the production tenant in the production system you
    • Import the forwarded situation type
    • Enter the appropriate values for the condition filters
    • Enable the situation type

Transports in 3-System-Landscape

Detailed Activation of a Situation Type in 3SL

Now let’s check the detailed steps for a sample use case in a 3-system-landscape as it is more comprehensive. In 2SL the export / import mechanism resembles the one from development system to test system in 3SL.

Depending on your system setting, the transports may also be processed automatically. For optimal clarity, the blog post discusses the transport steps through manual triggers.

Development System

Create a Situation Type from a Situation Template

Log-in as business process configuration expert on the customizing tenant in the development system. Open the Manage Situation Types – Extended app where you see a list of SAP delivered templates. Use the search option to find the template for our use case Expiration of Purchase Contracts (PROC_ABOUT_TO_EXPIRE_CTR). Select the template and an object page opens. In the header, select Create Situation Type.

Create situation type from situation template

A new page opens with the situation type that contains all information from the situation template. You just need to enter an ID, Name and Description. The type is configured and ready to use. Depending on your requirements you could adapt the settings, for example, by adding filter values for the conditions, changing texts or rescheduling the batch job.

I recommend monitoring the instances to see how situations are handled.

Monitor situations

Let’s check the relevant settings and understand how the configuration works.

There are two Situation Triggers that detect situations and cover different usage scenarios. While the batch-based trigger checks for situations in the background, the event-based trigger reacts on every active change of the contract.

Situation triggers

The situation triggers cover the following cases:

  • The Event-Based Trigger checks the conditions whenever you create or update a purchase contract.
    • Condition 1 checks if the validity period of a purchase contract expires within the next 30 days and triggers a situation. The information displayed to the user is defined in Situation Display number 1.
    • Condition 2 is only executed if condition 1 did not match. That is, the validity period is not within the next 30 days, for instance when the contract got extended, and the situation is closed. As nobody will be informed about the closure, the texts are empty (Situation Display number 2).

Event-based trigger

  • In addition to the events, the Batch-Based Trigger regularly checks the validity end date according to the batch schedule.
    • Condition 1 checks if the validity period of a purchase contract expires within the next 30 days and triggers a situation.

Batch-based trigger

The configuration for the Batch Job Scheduling specifies that the contract dates are verified every 3 hours throughout the day, beginning at 6:00 a.m.

Batch job scheduling

Export the Situation Type

Log-in as administrator on the customizing tenant in the development system. Open the Export Software Collection app.

  • On top of the table choose Create Software Collection and a new page opens
  • Choose Add Items and select the situation type you created
  • On the header select Check and wait until the check is processed successfully
  • Then choose Export and wait until the export is finished successfully

Test System

Import the Situation Type

Log-in as administrator on the test tenant in the test system. Open the Import Collection app.

  • Choose your software collection and a new page opens
  • On the header select Manual Import and wait until the check is processed successfully
  • Then choose Import on the bottom and wait until the import is finished successfully

Test the Situation Type

As business process specialist you can test the situation type on the corresponding tenant.

Make sure that the situation type is enabled.

Activate the situation type

Then maintain the conditions. The filter values are not transported since they may differ in the various systems and tenants.

  • Select the Event-Based Trigger and a new page opens
    • Condition 1 select Edit and enter the filter values
      • Ext. Reference ID: enter Empty, using the value help
      • Validity Period End: enter Next30Days, using the value help
    • Condition 2 select Edit and enter the filter values
      • Ext. Reference ID: enter Empty, using the value help
    • Go back to the main page

Event-based trigger

  • Select the Batch-Based Trigger and a new page opens
    • Condition 1 select Edit and enter the filter values
      • Ext. Reference ID: enter Empty, using the value help
      • Validity Period End: enter Next30Days, using the value help
    • Go back to the main page

Batch-based trigger

With the situation triggers, you defined when a situation is detected. Now, you need to define who should be informed about situations. Maintain the team(s) in the Manage Teams and Responsibilities app and ensure that at least one team is enabled. The filter settings work the same way as with the standard framework for Situation Handling.

Situation recipients

Now you can test the situation type in your business area with the corresponding application data. You can check if there are purchase contracts that match the conditions by choosing Trigger Batch and Manage Instances.

Test the type with trigger batch

If no situations were detected you can log-in as purchaser and create or manipulate a purchasing contract. Add an end date within the next 30 days and the save event will trigger a situation.

When you log-in as a team member of the recipients team you can also check, if you were alerted about the situation.

After the successful test you push the situation type to the production system.

Forward the Situation Type

Log-in as administrator and open the Import Collection app.

  • Select your software collection and a new page opens
  • On the header select Forward and wait until the validation is processed successfully
  • Then choose Forward on the bottom and wait until the export is finished successfully

Production System

Import Collection to Production System

As administrator open the Import Collection app on the production tenant in the production system.

  • Choose your software collection and a new page opens
  • On the header select Manual Import and wait until the check is processed successfully
  • Then choose Import on the bottom and wait until the import is finished successfully

Activate the Situation Type

Log-in as business process specialist and open the Manage Situation Types – Extended app. Like in the test system, you need to maintain the situation type.

  • Enable the situation type
  • Add the filter values for the trigger conditions
  • Ensure that at least one recipient team is enabled

Now you are all set.
